arxiv-2105-03316.title: Multi-Task Learning of Query Intent and Named Entities using Transfer Learning
arxiv-2105-03316.creator: Shalin Shah {shalin.shah@target.com}
arxiv-2105-03316.description: Abstract Named entity recognition (NER) has been studied extensively and the earlier algorithms were based on sequence labeling like Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and conditional random fields (CRF). These were followed by neural network based deep learning models. Recently, BERT has shown new state of the art accuracy in sequence labeling tasks like NER.

arxiv-2107-11393.title: 2M17091769+3127589: a mass-transfer binary with an extreme mass ratio PHOEBE ( Conroy et al. 2020 ) , GaussPy ( Lindner et al. 2015 ) , The Joker ( Price-Whelan et al. 2017 ) , eleanor ( Feinstein et al. 2019 ) , TOPCAT ( Taylor 2005 ) MESA; Version 12115; ( Paxton et al. 2011 ; Paxton et al. 2013 ;
arxiv-2107-11393.creator: Annaliese Miller, Marina Kounkel, Meng Sun(孙萌), Don Dixon, Chase Boggio, K. R. Covey, Keivan G. Stassun, Robert Mathieu
arxiv-2107-11393.description: Abstract We present the orbital solution of a peculiar double-lined spectroscopic and eclipsing binary system, 2M17091769+3127589. This solution was obtained by a simultaneous fit of both APOGEE radial velocities and TESS and ASAS-SN light curves to determine masses and radii. This system consists of an M = 0.256 − 0.006 + 0.010 M=0.256^{+0.010}_{-0.006} M ⊙ M_{\odot} , R = 3.

arxiv-2206-04627.title: Gaussian Process Model for the Local Stellar Velocity Field from Gaia Data Release 2 2022 Gaussian Process Model for the Local Stellar Velocity Field from Gaia Data Release 2 – References
arxiv-2206-04627.creator: Patrick Nelson, Lawrence M. Widrow
arxiv-2206-04627.description: Abstract We model the local stellar velocity field using position and velocity measurements for 4M stars from the second data release of Gaia . We determine the components of the mean or bulk velocity in ∼ 27 ​ k \sim 27k spatially-defined bins.

arxiv-2209-14841.title: Comparison of long-range corrected kernels and range-separated hybrids for excitons in solids
arxiv-2209-14841.creator: Rita Maji, Elena Degoli, Monica Calatayud, Valérie Véniard, Eleonora Luppi
arxiv-2209-14841.description: Abstract The most accurate theoretical method to describe excitons is the solution of the Bethe-Salpeter equation in the GW approximation (GW-BSE). However, because of its computation cost time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is becoming the alternative approach to GW-BSE to describe excitons in solids.

arxiv-2301-10732.title: An Efficient Semi-Automated Scheme for Infrastructure LiDAR Annotation Thanks: indicates corresponding author: Pan He (mybestsonny@gmail.com)
arxiv-2301-10732.creator: Aotian Wu, Pan He, Xiao Li, Ke Chen, Sanjay Ranka, Anand RangarajanModern Artificial Intelligence and Learning Technologies LabDepartment of Computer and Information Science and EngineeringThe University of Florida, Gainesville, Florida, USA
arxiv-2301-10732.description: Abstract Most existing perception systems rely on sensory data acquired from cameras, which perform poorly in low light and adverse weather conditions. To resolve this limitation, we have witnessed advanced LiDAR sensors become popular in perception tasks in autonomous driving applications. Nevertheless, their usage in traffic monitoring systems is less ubiquitous.

arxiv-2307-06870.title: Embodied Lifelong Learning for Task and Motion Planning
arxiv-2307-06870.creator: Jorge Mendez-Mendez, Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Tomás Lozano-Pérez
arxiv-2307-06870.description: Abstract A robot deployed in a home over long stretches of time faces a true lifelong learning problem. As it seeks to provide assistance to its users, the robot should leverage any accumulated experience to improve its own knowledge and proficiency.

arxiv-2404-05475.title: Linear Contextual Metaprogramming and Session Types
arxiv-2404-05475.creator: Pedro Ângelo, Atsushi Igarashi, Vasco T. Vasconcelos
arxiv-2404-05475.description: Abstract We explore the integration of metaprogramming in a call-by-value linear lambda-calculus and sketch its extension to a session type system. We build on a model of contextual modal type theory with multi-level contexts, where contextual values, closing arbitrary terms over a series of variables, may then be boxed and transmitted in messages.

arxiv-2506-20877.title: ThirdEye: Cue - Aware Monocular Depth Estimation via Brain - Inspired Multi - Stage Fusion
arxiv-2506-20877.creator: Calin Teodor Ioan
arxiv-2506-20877.description: Abstract Monocular depth estimation methods traditionally rely on deep learning models to implicitly understand complex depth features directly from RGB pixels. However, this approach often neglects explicit monocular cues that the human visual system naturally exploits—such as occlusion boundaries, shading patterns, and perspective layouts.

pmc-10523825.title: Effective Delivery of Vagus Nerve Stimulation Requires Many Stimulations Per Session and Many Sessions Per Week Over Many Weeks to Improve Recovery of Somatosensation
pmc-10523825.creator: Andrea D. Ruiz, Kaitlyn M. Malley, Tanya T. Danaphongse, Fatima N. Ahmad, Clareth Mota Beltran, Robert L. Rennaker, Michael P. Kilgard, Seth A. Hays
pmc-10523825.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundChronic sensory loss is a common and undertreated consequence of many forms of neurological injury. Emerging evidence indicates that vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) delivered during tactile rehabilitation promotes recovery of somatosensation.ObjectiveHere, we characterize the amount, intensity, frequency, and duration of VNS therapy paradigms to determine the optimal dosage for VNS-dependent enhancement of recovery in a model of peripheral nerve injury (PNI).MethodsRats underwent transection of the medial and ulnar nerves in the forelimb, resulting in chronic sensory loss in the paw.

pmc-10533293.title: Clinical and Biological Characteristics of Severe Malaria in Children under 5 Years Old in Benin
pmc-10533293.creator: Xiao Ma, Xin Fan, Kora Chabi Youssaou, Junfei Zhang, Xingyi Wang, Guoqiang Zheng, Shuping Tian, Yujing Gao
pmc-10533293.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background Malaria is a global public health concern, mainly occurring in sub-Saharan Africa. Children infected with malaria are more likely to develop severe disease, which can be fatal. During COVID-19 in 2020, diagnosing and treating malaria became difficult. We analyzed the clinical characteristics and laboratory indicators of children with severe malaria in Benin to provide important information for designing effective prevention and treatment strategies to manage pediatric cases.

pmc-10538450.title: Knockdown of PAF1 reduces cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration and invasion via retarding FLOT2-mediated MEK/ERK1/2 pathway
pmc-10538450.creator: Bin Tang, Shulan Dou
pmc-10538450.description: Cervical cancer (CC) is a very usual reproductive malignant tumor in women. RNA polymerase II-associated factor 1 (PAF1) and flotillin-2 (FLOT2) both have been discovered to key participators in cancers’ progression. However, the effects of PAF1/FLOT2 axis on CC development have not been probed.

pmc-11286312.title: A bilayer bioengineered patch with sequential dual-growth factor release to promote vascularization in bladder reconstruction
pmc-11286312.creator: Jian Zhao, Haoqian Zhang, Zhengyun Ling, Ziyan An, Shuwei Xiao, Pengchao Wang, Zhouyang Fu, Jinpeng Shao, Yanfeng Sun, Weijun Fu
pmc-11286312.description: Bladder tissue engineering holds promise for addressing bladder defects resulting from congenital or acquired bladder diseases. However, inadequate vascularization significantly impacts the survival and function of engineered tissues after transplantation. Herein, a novel bilayer silk fibroin (BSF) scaffold was fabricated with the capability of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) sequential release.

pmc-11353766.title: Genetic and Phenotypic Spectrum of KMT2D Variants in Taiwanese Case Series of Kabuki Syndrome
pmc-11353766.creator: Chung-Lin Lee, Chih-Kuang Chuang, Ming-Ren Chen, Ju-Li Lin, Huei-Ching Chiu, Ya-Hui Chang, Yuan-Rong Tu, Yun-Ting Lo, Hsiang-Yu Lin, Shuan-Pei Lin, Benedetta Nacmias
pmc-11353766.description: Kabuki syndrome (KS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by distinct facial features, intellectual disability, and multiple congenital anomalies. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of KS in a Taiwanese patient group of 23 patients. KMT2D variants were found in 22 individuals, with missense (26.1%), nonsense (21.7%), and frameshift (17.4%) variants being the most prevalent.

pmc-11692670.title: SUBJECTIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE AND RISK OF MORTALITY AMONG BEREAVED PARENTS IN OLD AGE
pmc-11692670.creator: Jieun Song, Seung Eun Cha, Carol Ryff
pmc-11692670.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The death of a child is a highly traumatic event that may impact the subsequent health of parents. Prior research shows greater risk of early deaths in bereaved parents relative to non-bereaved parents. This study examined whether the associations between the death of a child and parents’ mortality risk are mediated by subjective cognitive decline (SCD), known to be predictive of mortality and Alzheimer’s disease, contingent on parents’ age. The analytic sample consists of participants in Midlife in the U.S.

pmc-11714257.title: The association of birth in the Stroke Belt and neuroimaging brain biomarkers in a cohort of older Black Americans
pmc-11714257.creator: Yi Lor, Kristen M George, Rachel Peterson, Sirena Gutierrez, Alexander Ivan B Posis, Charles Decarli, Lisa L Barnes, Paola Gilsanz, Rachel A Whitmer
pmc-11714257.description: BackgroundHaving ever lived in the southeastern United States, a region referred to as the Stroke Belt (SB), is associated with higher dementia incidence and poorer late‐life cognition. We assessed whether birth in the SB was associated with late‐life MRI‐based regional brain volumes among racially/ethnically diverse older adults who are long‐term residents of Northern California.

pmc-12587421.title: Single-nuclei sequencing of Moricandia arvensis reveals bundle sheath cell function in the photorespiratory shuttle of C3-C4 intermediate Brassicaceae
pmc-12587421.creator: Sebastian Triesch, Vanessa Reichel-Deland, José Miguel Valderrama Martín, Michael Melzer, Urte Schlüter, Andreas P M Weber
pmc-12587421.description: Spatially confined gene expression determines cell identity and is fundamental to complex plant traits. In the evolutionary transition from C3 to the more efficient C4 photosynthesis, restricting the glycine decarboxylase reaction to bundle sheath cells initiates a carbon concentrating mechanism via the photorespiratory glycine shuttle.

pmc-12840188.title: Dynamic Synchronization and Resonance as the Origin of 1/f Fluctuations—Amplitude Modulation Across Music and Nature
pmc-12840188.creator: Akika Nakamichi, Izumi Uesaka, Masahiro Morikawa
pmc-12840188.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In natural systems, astrophysics, biological physics, and social physics, 1/f fluctuations are observed across a wide range of systems. Focusing on the case of music, we propose and verify a physical mechanism for generating these fluctuations. This mechanism is based on amplitude modulation (AM) and demodulation (DM), where the 1/f spectral law appears not in the raw waveform but in its demodulated amplitude envelope.

pmc-12971378.title: VV‐ECMO Combined With M‐TEER for the Treatment of Mitral Valve Papillary Muscle Rupture Following Acute Myocardial Infarction PCI: A Case Report
pmc-12971378.creator: Zhenjiang Liu
pmc-12971378.description: Mitral valve papillary muscle rupture represents a rare yet critical complication of acute myocardial infarction, often leading to severe mitral regurgitation and subsequent pulmonary edema with high mortality. Despite optimal ventilatory support and pharmacological management, patients often exhibit refractory hypoxemia, rendering surgical intervention both technically demanding and high‐risk.

pmc-13176806.title: Examining the Relationship Between Early Feeding Difficulties and Language Development: A Longitudinal Study
pmc-13176806.creator: Simone Poulin, David H. McFarland, Stefano Rezzonico, Natacha Trudeau
pmc-13176806.description: Increasing evidence suggests that interactive feeding is an important variable in language development, with early disruptions in feeding potentially having long‐term consequences. This longitudinal experiment characterized early patterns of feeding difficulties and language development in full‐term, typically‐developing infants across the developmental milestones of 8, 12, 18, 24, and 54 months.

pmc-13351278.title: Metabolomic data of melittin-intervened murine cervical cancer cells based on liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
pmc-13351278.creator: Jianrong Jiang, Yaqin Gao, Mengyi Wang, Ronghua Zhang, Jiwu Lou, Yueliang Li, Jianfeng Qiu, Dafu Chen, Tizhen Yan, Rui Guo, Yanhui Liu
pmc-13351278.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Melittin-treated murine cervical cancer U14 cells have been widely recognized as a classic cellular model for anti-tumor research in cervical cancer. This article contains metabolomic data of U14 cell lysates from both melittin-treated and control groups. Untargeted metabolomic profiling was carried out by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to systematically elucidate the global metabolic disturbances in cervical cancer cells upon melittin intervention. LC-MS raw data were processed for peak extraction and alignment using XCMS software, followed by quality control normalization with metaX software.

pmc-13416087.title: Donor dependency and pandemic readiness: insights from the 2026 Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the East African community
pmc-13416087.creator: John Mugisha, Julius Niyibizi, Emmanuel Nizeyimana, Munawar Harun Koray
pmc-13416087.description: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak has exposed persistent weaknesses in health-security preparedness across the East African Community (EAC). Although regional preparedness has improved, major gaps remain in early detection, cross-border collaboration and surveillance, laboratory capacity, infection prevention and control, and community engagement.
